text: {"answerable": false, "answer": "The passages do not include the SchNet paper itself, so they do not say which kernel method it compared against on MD17. They do cover NequIP against kernel methods: it significantly outperforms kernel-based approaches such as GAP, FCHL19/GPR and sGDML on MD-17 [W4225405705#010]. The NewtonNet table is consistent with this for sGDML. NequIP's force MAE is lower than sGDML's on aspirin (0.348 vs 0.68), naphthalene, salicylic acid and toluene, but higher on ethanol (0.208 vs 0.33 is lower, while FCHL19 gets 0.136) and malonaldehyde (0.337 vs 0.41 is lower, while FCHL19 gets 0.245) [W3189651386#010]. NequIP is therefore not uniformly best against every kernel method in that table."}
